stories.title: China media hails Canada’s ‘Chinese-style’ tariff retaliation
stories.summary: China's Global Times praised Canada’s tariff retaliation against the US as a "Chinese-style counter attack" validating opposition to US protectionism. The US plans 50% tariffs on $20 billion of Canadian goods; Canada will retaliate dollar-for-dollar starting September 8. China-Canada relations have warmed with new trade agreements and possible high-level visits, marking a shift from previous tensions. China’s nationalist tabloid Global Times praised Canada’s retaliation against US tariffs, casting Ottawa’s move as validating Beijing’s opposition to Washington’s protectionist trade policies. Calling Canada’s action “Chinese-style counter attack,” the newspaper said in an editorial on Aug 24 that the government’s decision shows that “more countries are realising that concessions toward the US do not necessarily bring respect and stability.” Canada walked away from trade negotiations with the US over the weekend, with both sides blaming the other for last-minute changes. The Global Times cited US trade representative Jamieson Greer’s comparison of Canada’s measures to “the kind of things that China would do.” That remark amounted to an acknowledgement of “the failure of US policy,” the newspaper said. The editorial argued that the dispute demonstrated that US allies aren’t exempt from Washington’s use of tariffs. “Today it is Canada; tomorrow it could be the EU, and the day after, Japan or South Korea,” it said. Beijing has sought to cast its own retaliation against previous US tariffs as a matter of reciprocity and a defence of the international trading system. China and the US agreed to a trade truce after several rounds of negotiations, though tensions have persisted over technology and other economic restrictions.

stories.title: Japan accelerates line toward militarization — DPRK
stories.summary: PYONGYANG, August 24. Japan is accelerating its line toward militarization and creating conditions for further expansion of its military capabilities, the Korean Central News Agency (KCNA) reported. The authors of the report highlighted the events held on August 15 at Tokyo’s Yasukuni Shrine, which is viewed in North Korea and several other Asian countries as a symbol of militarism. Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi previously sent a ritual offering to the shrine. Pyongyang links the move to Tokyo’s military policy, specifically, the deployment of preemptive strike capabilities, plans to ease arms export restrictions, and a potential revision of Japan’s policy against possessing, producing, or hosting nuclear weapons.
